descriptors.title: Growing patterns with rational numbers
descriptors.description: Recognise and use rules that generate visually growing patterns and number patterns involving rational numbers

nodes.label: Identifying rules in number patterns
nodes.checkpoint: Students can identify the rule governing a number pattern involving rational numbers and use it to extend the pattern.
criteria: Student identifies the rule for a number pattern involving rational numbers and states it clearly.
Student extends the pattern correctly using the identified rule.

nodes.label: Visually growing patterns and their rules
nodes.checkpoint: Students can describe the rule for a visually growing pattern using numbers, identify the connection between the visual structure and the number sequence, and use the rule to predict future terms.
criteria: Student describes the rule for a visually growing pattern as a number sequence.
Student uses the rule to predict the number of elements in a non-adjacent term.

nodes.label: Generating and representing patterns
nodes.checkpoint: Students can create a number pattern from a given rule involving rational numbers and represent it in multiple forms (table of values, number sequence, visual pattern where applicable).
criteria: Student generates a number pattern from a given rule involving rational numbers.
Student represents the pattern in at least two forms (e.g. sequence and table).

descriptors.title: Unknown values with brackets
descriptors.description: Find unknown values in numerical equations involving brackets and combinations of arithmetic operations, using the properties of numbers and operations

nodes.label: Order of operations including brackets
nodes.checkpoint: Students can evaluate numerical expressions involving brackets and combinations of operations, applying order-of-operations conventions correctly.
criteria: Student correctly evaluates expressions involving brackets and mixed operations.
Student explains why bracket placement changes the result of an expression.

nodes.label: Finding unknown values in equations with brackets
nodes.checkpoint: Students can find unknown values in numerical equations involving brackets and combinations of operations by applying inverse operations and number properties systematically.
criteria: Student correctly finds the unknown in an equation with brackets using inverse operations.
Student verifies the solution by substituting back into the original equation.

nodes.label: Using number properties to solve and simplify
nodes.checkpoint: Students can apply number properties (distributive, associative, commutative) to simplify expressions and solve equations involving brackets and combinations of operations.
criteria: Student applies the distributive property to expand or simplify a bracketed expression.
Student uses at least one number property to simplify a calculation and names the property used.

descriptors.title: Algorithms for number patterns
descriptors.description: Create and use algorithms involving a sequence of steps and decisions that use rules to generate sets of numbers; identify, interpret and explain emerging patterns

nodes.label: What an algorithm is — steps and decisions
nodes.checkpoint: Students can describe an algorithm as a precise sequence of steps, including conditional decisions, that can be followed to produce a result.
criteria: Student identifies the steps and at least one decision point in a given algorithm.
Student follows a simple algorithm to produce its output.

nodes.label: Creating algorithms to generate number sets
nodes.checkpoint: Students can create an algorithm (as written steps or a flowchart) that uses a rule to generate a set of numbers, and use it to produce the set.
criteria: Student creates an algorithm with at least three steps and one decision point that generates a number set.
Student traces through the algorithm to verify it produces the correct set.

nodes.label: Identifying and explaining emerging patterns
nodes.checkpoint: Students can use an algorithm to generate a set of numbers, identify patterns that emerge in the set, and explain why those patterns arise from the algorithm's rules.
criteria: Student identifies a pattern in a number set generated by an algorithm.
Student explains why the pattern arises by referring to the rule in the algorithm.

descriptors.title: Convert metric units
descriptors.description: Convert between common metric units of length, mass and capacity; choose and use decimal representations of metric measurements relevant to the context of a problem

nodes.label: Metric conversion as powers-of-10 operation
nodes.checkpoint: Students can explain that metric conversions involve multiplying or dividing by powers of 10 and apply this to convert between adjacent metric units.
criteria: Student correctly converts between adjacent metric units across at least two measurement types.
Student states the conversion factor and whether to multiply or divide for a given conversion.

nodes.label: Decimal representations of metric measurements
nodes.checkpoint: Students can express metric measurements using decimal notation and choose the representation most relevant to the context.
criteria: Student converts a two-unit metric measurement to a decimal representation in the larger unit.
Student selects an appropriate representation for a given problem context and explains the choice.

nodes.label: Metric conversions in problem solving
nodes.checkpoint: Students can identify when unit conversion is necessary to solve a problem, perform the conversion, and use the result appropriately.
criteria: Student identifies that a conversion is needed before solving a problem and performs it correctly.
Student uses the converted value to complete the calculation and expresses the answer in appropriate units.

descriptors.title: Area of rectangles
descriptors.description: Establish the formula for the area of a rectangle and use it to solve practical problems

nodes.label: Establishing the area formula
nodes.checkpoint: Students can explain why the area of a rectangle is length × width by connecting the formula to the array structure of square unit counting.
criteria: Student explains why area = length × width using an array or row-counting argument.
Student applies the formula to find the area of a rectangle with given dimensions.

nodes.label: Area with decimal and fractional dimensions
nodes.checkpoint: Students can apply the area formula to rectangles with decimal dimensions and interpret the result in appropriate square units.
criteria: Student correctly calculates the area of a rectangle with decimal dimensions and states the appropriate unit.
Student identifies and corrects a unit error in a given area calculation.

nodes.label: Area in practical problem contexts
nodes.checkpoint: Students can formulate and solve practical problems requiring the area of a rectangle, including problems requiring decomposition of irregular shapes into rectangles.
criteria: Student solves a practical area problem showing dimensions, formula, calculation, and units.
Student correctly finds a missing dimension when area and one side are given.

descriptors.title: Angle relationships
descriptors.description: Identify the relationships between angles on a straight line, angles at a point and vertically opposite angles; use these to determine unknown angles, communicating reasoning

nodes.label: Angles on a straight line
nodes.checkpoint: Students can identify that angles on a straight line sum to 180° and use this to find an unknown angle.
criteria: Student states the angle relationship for angles on a straight line.
Student correctly finds an unknown angle on a straight line and explains the reasoning.

nodes.label: Angles at a point
nodes.checkpoint: Students can identify that angles at a point sum to 360° and use this to find unknown angles.
criteria: Student states the angle relationship for angles at a point.
Student correctly finds an unknown angle at a point and shows the calculation.

nodes.label: Vertically opposite angles
nodes.checkpoint: Students can identify vertically opposite angles in a diagram and use the property that they are equal to find unknown angles.
criteria: Student identifies vertically opposite angle pairs in a diagram.
Student uses the property to find unknown angles and explains why the angles are equal.

nodes.label: Combining angle relationships to solve problems
nodes.checkpoint: Students can identify which angle relationships apply in a multi-step diagram and use a combination of relationships to find multiple unknown angles, communicating their reasoning.
criteria: Student correctly finds all unknown angles in a diagram using at least two different angle relationships.
Student communicates the reasoning, naming the relationship used at each step.

descriptors.title: Integers and Cartesian plane
descriptors.description: Recognise situations, including financial contexts, that use integers; locate and represent integers on a number line and as coordinates on the Cartesian plane

nodes.label: Meaning of integers
nodes.checkpoint: Students can explain what integers are, distinguish positive and negative integers from whole numbers, and give real-world examples of situations where negative integers are necessary.
criteria: Student identifies at least two real-world situations where negative integers are needed and explains what zero represents in each.
Student distinguishes between situations requiring only whole numbers and those requiring integers.

nodes.label: Integers on a number line
nodes.checkpoint: Students can locate and represent positive and negative integers on a number line, order integers including negative values, and describe the distance between integers.
criteria: Student correctly places positive and negative integers on a number line, including values between labelled intervals.
Student orders a set of integers including negative values from least to greatest and explains why a negative integer with larger absolute value is the lesser number.

nodes.label: Integer coordinates — first quadrant extension
nodes.checkpoint: Students can extend their understanding of grid coordinates to include negative values on both axes and locate points with integer coordinates in all four quadrants of the Cartesian plane.
criteria: Student correctly plots points with integer coordinates in all four quadrants.
Student reads coordinates of points in all four quadrants and correctly reports the sign of each value.
Student explains what it means for a coordinate to be negative (direction from origin).

nodes.label: Integers in financial and real-world modelling
nodes.checkpoint: Students can recognise and use integers in financial contexts, represent financial situations on number lines, and interpret positive and negative integer values in terms of the situation.
criteria: Student correctly represents a financial situation (credits and debits, or profit and loss) using positive and negative integers.
Student interprets what a positive, zero, and negative result means in a specific financial context.

descriptors.title: Prime, composite and square numbers
descriptors.description: Identify and describe the properties of prime, composite and square numbers and use these properties to solve problems and simplify calculations

nodes.label: Factors and the prime/composite distinction
nodes.checkpoint: Students can determine the number of factors a whole number has and classify it as prime (exactly two factors: 1 and itself) or composite (more than two factors).
criteria: Student correctly identifies all factors of a given number to 100 and classifies it as prime or composite.
Student explains why 1 is neither prime nor composite and why 2 is the only even prime.

nodes.label: Prime factorisation
nodes.checkpoint: Students can express composite numbers as products of prime factors using factor trees or repeated division.
criteria: Student correctly constructs a factor tree for a composite number and expresses the result as a product of primes.
Student verifies their prime factorisation by multiplication.

nodes.label: Square numbers and their properties
nodes.checkpoint: Students can identify square numbers, recognise them as products of a number multiplied by itself, connect them to square arrays, and identify square roots of familiar square numbers.
criteria: Student correctly identifies whether a given number is a square number and explains why using an array or multiplication.
Student states the square root of familiar square numbers up to 144.

nodes.label: Using number properties to simplify and solve
nodes.checkpoint: Students can use properties of prime, composite and square numbers to solve problems and simplify calculations, including selecting efficient approaches.
criteria: Student uses number property knowledge (prime, composite, or square) to select an efficient approach to at least one problem and explains their reasoning.
Student correctly applies the chosen strategy and verifies the answer.

descriptors.title: Compare and order fractions
descriptors.description: Apply knowledge of equivalence to compare, order and represent common fractions including halves, thirds and quarters on the same number line and justify their order

nodes.label: Equivalence as the comparison tool
nodes.checkpoint: Students can explain why equivalent fractions are needed to compare fractions with different denominators, and generate equivalent fractions for common fractions by multiplying or dividing numerator and denominator by the same factor.
criteria: Student generates three equivalent fractions for a given common fraction and explains why they are equal.
Student verifies equivalence using a diagram or number line representation.

nodes.label: Common denominator for comparison
nodes.checkpoint: Students can find a common denominator for two or more fractions with different denominators and use it to determine which is greater.
criteria: Student correctly finds a common denominator for two fractions with different denominators.
Student converts both fractions correctly and identifies which is greater.

nodes.label: Order fractions on a number line
nodes.checkpoint: Students can order three or more common fractions including halves, thirds and quarters on the same number line and justify the ordering using equivalence.
criteria: Student correctly orders at least five common fractions on a number line.
Student justifies the ordering of at least two fractions using equivalence reasoning (not just 'the number is bigger').

descriptors.title: Add and subtract decimals
descriptors.description: Apply knowledge of place value to add and subtract decimals, using digital tools where appropriate; use estimation and rounding to check the reasonableness of answers

nodes.label: Place value alignment for decimal operations
nodes.checkpoint: Students can align decimal numbers by place value to set up addition and subtraction calculations, including numbers with different numbers of decimal places.
criteria: Student correctly aligns decimal numbers for calculation, including adding placeholder zeros where needed.
Student explains why alignment ensures correct place value combinations.

nodes.label: Adding and subtracting decimals
nodes.checkpoint: Students can accurately add and subtract decimal numbers with up to three decimal places using written and mental strategies.
criteria: Student accurately adds and subtracts decimal numbers with up to two decimal places using a written strategy.
Student identifies and corrects a calculation error in a provided worked example.

nodes.label: Estimation and rounding as a reasonableness check
nodes.checkpoint: Students can round decimal numbers to check the reasonableness of addition and subtraction results, and identify when a calculated answer is unreasonable.
criteria: Student uses rounding to estimate a decimal sum or difference and compares the estimate to their calculated answer.
Student identifies whether a given calculated answer is reasonable using estimation and explains their reasoning.

descriptors.title: Add and subtract fractions
descriptors.description: Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions using knowledge of equivalent fractions

nodes.label: Finding a common denominator for calculation
nodes.checkpoint: Students can find a common denominator for fractions with unrelated denominators and convert both fractions before adding or subtracting.
criteria: Student correctly finds a common denominator for two fractions with different denominators.
Student converts both fractions correctly and calculates the sum or difference.

nodes.label: Adding and subtracting mixed numerals
nodes.checkpoint: Students can add and subtract mixed numerals, managing the conversion between mixed numerals and improper fractions where needed.
criteria: Student adds two mixed numerals with different denominators correctly.
Student subtracts mixed numerals including cases requiring regrouping.

nodes.label: Fraction addition and subtraction in problems
nodes.checkpoint: Students can solve contextual problems that require adding and subtracting fractions, selecting appropriate strategies and interpreting results.
criteria: Student correctly solves a word problem involving addition or subtraction of fractions with different denominators, showing the common denominator step.
Student interprets the answer in the context of the problem.

descriptors.title: Multiply and divide decimals
descriptors.description: Multiply and divide decimals by multiples of powers of 10 without a calculator, applying knowledge of place value and proficiency with multiplication facts; using estimation and rounding to check the reasonableness of answers

nodes.label: Multiplying decimals by powers of 10
nodes.checkpoint: Students can multiply decimal numbers by 10, 100 and 1000 by shifting digits to the left, and explain the effect in terms of place value.
criteria: Student correctly multiplies a decimal number by 10, 100 and 1000 and states the resulting number.
Student explains the place value change that occurs when multiplying by a power of 10.

nodes.label: Dividing decimals by powers of 10
nodes.checkpoint: Students can divide decimal numbers by 10, 100 and 1000 by shifting digits to the right, and explain the effect in terms of place value.
criteria: Student correctly divides a decimal number by 10, 100 and 1000.
Student explains the relationship between multiplying and dividing by the same power of 10 as inverse operations.

nodes.label: Multiplying by multiples of powers of 10
nodes.checkpoint: Students can multiply and divide decimals by multiples of powers of 10 (e.g. 200, 0.5, 3000) by decomposing the multiplier and applying place value knowledge.
criteria: Student multiplies a decimal by a multiple of a power of 10 showing the two-step decomposition.
Student uses estimation to verify the reasonableness of a multiplication or division result.

descriptors.title: Fractions, decimals and percentages
descriptors.description: Solve problems that require finding a familiar fraction, decimal or percentage of a quantity, including percentage discounts, choosing efficient calculation strategies and using digital tools where appropriate

nodes.label: Finding a fraction of a quantity
nodes.checkpoint: Students can find a unit fraction and non-unit fraction of a whole number or measurement quantity using multiplication and division.
criteria: Student correctly finds a unit fraction of a quantity using division.
Student extends to non-unit fractions using the divide-then-multiply method.

nodes.label: Finding a percentage of a quantity
nodes.checkpoint: Students can find common percentages (10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 20%) of a quantity using efficient strategies connecting percentages to fraction and decimal equivalents.
criteria: Student finds 50%, 25%, and 10% of a given quantity using a mental or written strategy.
Student explains the connection between the percentage and the calculation method used.

nodes.label: Percentage discounts and financial applications
nodes.checkpoint: Students can calculate a percentage discount on a price and determine the discounted price.
criteria: Student correctly calculates a percentage discount and determines the discounted price.
Student explains the two steps: finding the discount amount and subtracting from the original price.

descriptors.title: Approximate with rational numbers
descriptors.description: Approximate numerical solutions to problems involving rational numbers and percentages, including financial contexts, using appropriate estimation strategies

nodes.label: Rounding rational numbers for estimation
nodes.checkpoint: Students can round fractions, decimals and percentages to convenient values to produce estimates, selecting the rounding precision appropriate to the context.
criteria: Student rounds decimals and fractions to convenient values and uses them to produce a reasonable estimate.
Student explains why their chosen rounding precision is appropriate for the context.

nodes.label: Benchmark and mental estimation strategies
nodes.checkpoint: Students can apply benchmark estimation strategies (using 0, ½, 1 as reference points; using 10% as a base for percentage estimates) to approximate rational number solutions.
criteria: Student applies at least two different estimation strategies to rational number problems and explains when each is useful.
Student uses estimation to check whether a calculated answer to a percentage or fraction problem is plausible.

nodes.label: Approximation in financial and real-world contexts
nodes.checkpoint: Students can select and apply appropriate estimation strategies to approximate solutions to problems involving rational numbers and percentages in financial and practical contexts.
criteria: Student selects an appropriate estimation strategy for a financial context problem and explains why it suits the situation.
Student communicates an approximate solution with an appropriate level of precision for the context.

descriptors.title: Model with rational numbers
descriptors.description: Use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving natural and rational numbers and percentages, including in financial contexts; formulate the problems, choosing operations and efficient calculation strategies, and using digital tools where appropriate; interpret and communicate solutions in terms of the situation, justifying the choices made

nodes.label: Formulating rational number problems
nodes.checkpoint: Students can identify the mathematical structure of a practical problem involving rational numbers or percentages and formulate it as a mathematical calculation.
criteria: Student writes a mathematical expression or equation that correctly represents the structure of a practical problem.
Student explains why they chose the operations they did.

nodes.label: Choosing efficient strategies and digital tools
nodes.checkpoint: Students can select efficient calculation strategies for rational number problems, including deciding when digital tools are appropriate, and execute the calculation accurately.
criteria: Student selects a strategy appropriate to the problem and explains their choice.
Student uses estimation to check that their answer is reasonable.

nodes.label: Interpreting and communicating solutions
nodes.checkpoint: Students can interpret the mathematical result of a rational number calculation in terms of the original situation and communicate the solution with appropriate precision and justification.
criteria: Student answers a practical problem with a complete contextual statement (not just a number).
Student justifies whether their answer is reasonable and whether any rounding decision was appropriate.

descriptors.title: Probability scale 0 to 1
descriptors.description: Recognise that probabilities lie on numerical scales of 0 – 1 or 0% – 100% and use estimation to assign probabilities that events occur in a given context, using common fractions, percentages and decimals

nodes.label: The probability scale
nodes.checkpoint: Students can place events on a 0–1 probability scale and connect impossible (0), certain (1), and unlikely/likely/even chance positions to their numerical values.
criteria: Student places at least three events at appropriate positions on a 0–1 probability scale with justification.
Student explains what 0, 1, and 0.5 represent on the scale.

nodes.label: Representing probability as fractions, decimals and percentages
nodes.checkpoint: Students can express the same probability value as a fraction, decimal, and percentage, and convert between these representations.
criteria: Student expresses a probability as a fraction, decimal, and percentage.
Student selects a representation appropriate to the context.

nodes.label: Estimating probabilities in context
nodes.checkpoint: Students can use estimation to assign reasonable probabilities to events in a given context, justifying their estimates using the 0–1 scale.
criteria: Student assigns reasonable estimated probabilities to events in a context and justifies the estimates.
Student checks that probabilities for complementary events sum to 1.

descriptors.title: Simulations with increasing trials
descriptors.description: Conduct repeated chance experiments and run simulations with an increasing number of trials using digital tools; compare observations with expected results and discuss the effect on variation of increasing the number of trials

nodes.label: Experimental vs theoretical probability
nodes.checkpoint: Students can distinguish between theoretical probability (what should happen) and experimental probability (what did happen), and recognise that they may differ in small samples.
criteria: Student calculates experimental probability from a set of trials.
Student compares experimental to theoretical probability and explains why they may differ.

nodes.label: Effect of increasing trials on variation
nodes.checkpoint: Students can describe how increasing the number of trials in a probability experiment reduces variation in the experimental probability estimate.
criteria: Student describes how experimental probability changes as the number of trials increases.
Student explains why more trials generally gives a more reliable estimate.

nodes.label: Digital simulations for large trial counts
nodes.checkpoint: Students can use digital tools to run simulations with large numbers of trials and use the results to compare experimental and expected outcomes.
criteria: Student runs a digital simulation and records experimental probabilities.
Student compares results from different trial sizes and describes the trend.

descriptors.title: Cross-sections and prisms
descriptors.description: Compare the parallel cross-sections of objects and recognise their relationships to right prisms

nodes.label: What a cross-section is
nodes.checkpoint: Students can describe a cross-section as a 2D slice through a 3D object and identify the shape of a cross-section from a given object.
criteria: Student describes a cross-section as a 2D slice through a 3D object.
Student correctly identifies the cross-sectional shape of at least two common objects.

nodes.label: Constant cross-sections and prisms
nodes.checkpoint: Students can identify objects whose parallel cross-sections are identical (constant) and connect this to the definition of a right prism.
criteria: Student identifies objects with constant parallel cross-sections and names them as prisms.
Student explains what distinguishes a prism from a non-prism using cross-section reasoning.

nodes.label: Comparing and classifying 3D objects by cross-section
nodes.checkpoint: Students can compare parallel cross-sections of different objects and use this comparison to classify and describe relationships between 3D shapes.
criteria: Student correctly classifies a set of 3D objects as prisms or non-prisms with cross-section justification.
Student describes how cross-sections differ between prisms and non-prisms.

descriptors.title: Cartesian plane — 4 quadrants
descriptors.description: Locate points in the 4 quadrants of a Cartesian plane; describe changes to the coordinates when a point is moved to a different position in the plane

nodes.label: Extending coordinates to all four quadrants
nodes.checkpoint: Students can identify and name the four quadrants of the Cartesian plane and locate points with integer coordinates in all four quadrants.
criteria: Student correctly plots points in all four quadrants.
Student reads coordinates of points in all quadrants and correctly identifies the quadrant from coordinate signs.

nodes.label: Describing coordinate changes when moving a point
nodes.checkpoint: Students can describe how the coordinates of a point change when it is translated horizontally, vertically, or diagonally in the Cartesian plane.
criteria: Student correctly identifies which coordinate changes when a point is moved horizontally or vertically.
Student predicts the new coordinates of a point after a described movement.

descriptors.title: Tessellations and transformations
descriptors.description: Recognise and use combinations of transformations to create tessellations and other geometric patterns, using dynamic geometric software where appropriate

nodes.label: Combining transformations
nodes.checkpoint: Students can apply a sequence of two or more transformations to a shape and describe the combined effect.
criteria: Student applies two transformations in sequence to a shape and correctly sketches the result.
Student describes each transformation in the sequence.

nodes.label: What makes a tessellation
nodes.checkpoint: Students can identify what properties of a shape and transformation allow it to tessellate (tile a plane without gaps or overlaps).
criteria: Student identifies whether a polygon tessellates and explains the reason using interior angles.
Student identifies the transformation(s) generating a given tessellation.

nodes.label: Creating tessellations and geometric patterns
nodes.checkpoint: Students can create a tessellation or geometric pattern using a specified combination of transformations and describe the rule generating the pattern.
criteria: Student creates a tessellation using a specified shape and transformation combination with no gaps or overlaps.
Student describes the transformation rule generating their tessellation.

descriptors.title: Compare distributions
descriptors.description: Interpret and compare data sets for ordinal and nominal categorical, discrete and continuous numerical variables using comparative displays or visualisations and digital tools; compare distributions in terms of mode, range and shape

nodes.label: Variable types and appropriate displays
nodes.checkpoint: Students can identify whether a variable is ordinal categorical, nominal categorical, discrete numerical, or continuous numerical and select an appropriate display for each.
criteria: Student correctly classifies a variable by type.
Student selects and justifies an appropriate display for a given variable type.

nodes.label: Mode, range and shape as comparative tools
nodes.checkpoint: Students can calculate or identify the mode and range of a data set and describe its shape, and use these to make comparative statements between two data sets.
criteria: Student identifies the mode, range, and shape of a dataset.
Student makes at least two specific comparative statements between two datasets using these measures.

nodes.label: Comparative displays and interpretation
nodes.checkpoint: Students can construct or read comparative displays (side-by-side bar charts, parallel dot plots) and use them to compare distributions, stating conclusions in the context of the data.
criteria: Student reads a comparative display and states two specific distributional differences between the datasets.
Student relates the statistical comparison to the context of the data (not just the numbers).

descriptors.title: Plan and refine investigations
descriptors.description: Plan and conduct statistical investigations by posing and refining questions or identifying a problem and collecting relevant data; analyse and interpret the data and communicate findings within the context of the investigation

nodes.label: Posing and refining the investigation question
nodes.checkpoint: Students can pose a statistical question for investigation, identify what data is needed, and refine the question based on feasibility or initial findings.
criteria: Student poses a statistical question and explains what data is needed to answer it.
Student identifies at least one way the question could be refined for better investigation.

nodes.label: Collecting and organising relevant data
nodes.checkpoint: Students can select and use data collection methods appropriate to their investigation question, collect data systematically, and organise it for analysis.
criteria: Student collects data using a method appropriate to the investigation question.
Student organises the data in a form that supports analysis.

nodes.label: Analysing, interpreting and communicating findings
nodes.checkpoint: Students can analyse collected data using appropriate measures and displays, interpret the findings in context, and communicate conclusions that address the original investigation question.
criteria: Student produces an appropriate display and states findings using statistical measures.
Student communicates conclusions that specifically address the original investigation question.

descriptors.title: Variables and formulas
descriptors.description: recognise and use variables to represent everyday formulas algebraically and substitute values into formulas to determine an unknown

nodes.label: Variables as generalised quantities
nodes.checkpoint: Students recognise that variables represent quantities that can change, and distinguish a variable from an unknown constant.
criteria: Correctly identifies what each variable represents in a given formula.
Explains the difference between a variable that can take many values and a specific unknown.
Does not treat all variables as things to 'solve for'.

nodes.label: Substituting values into formulas
nodes.checkpoint: Students substitute given numerical values into a formula and calculate the result.
criteria: Correctly substitutes values into a formula and evaluates.
Applies correct order of operations during substitution.
Does not multiply the coefficient by the variable label (e.g. does not treat 3A as 3×'the letter A' rather than 3 times the value of A).

nodes.label: Finding an unknown by substitution and backtracking
nodes.checkpoint: Students determine the value of an unknown variable in a formula by substituting known values and solving.
criteria: Correctly finds an unknown in a formula given all other values.
Verifies the solution by substituting back into the formula.
Interprets the result in context (with units and meaning).

descriptors.title: Algebraic expressions
descriptors.description: formulate algebraic expressions using constants, variables, operations and brackets

nodes.label: Translating words to algebraic expressions
nodes.checkpoint: Students translate verbal descriptions of mathematical relationships into algebraic expressions using constants, variables and operations.
criteria: Correctly translates a verbal description into an algebraic expression.
Correctly translates an algebraic expression into a verbal description.
Does not confuse 'n less than 5' (5 − n) with 'n minus 5' (n − 5).

nodes.label: Expressions with brackets and multiple operations
nodes.checkpoint: Students formulate algebraic expressions involving brackets, including those where brackets are required to preserve intended meaning.
criteria: Correctly writes expressions requiring brackets to preserve intended meaning.
Can explain why brackets are necessary in a given expression.
Evaluates expressions with brackets correctly applying order of operations.

nodes.label: Generalising arithmetic to algebraic expressions
nodes.checkpoint: Students recognise that algebraic expressions generalise arithmetic relationships, and can identify what an expression represents across multiple cases.
criteria: Writes an algebraic expression that correctly generalises a given arithmetic pattern.
Verifies the expression by substituting specific values.
Does not confuse the generalised expression with a specific equation to solve.

descriptors.title: Solve linear equations
descriptors.description: solve one-variable linear equations with natural number solutions; verify the solution by substitution

nodes.label: Equation as a balance statement
nodes.checkpoint: Students understand that an equation is a statement of equality and that the solution is the value that makes it true.
criteria: Correctly identifies whether a given value satisfies an equation by substitution.
Distinguishes between an expression and an equation.
Understands that a solution must make both sides equal.

nodes.label: Solving by backtracking
nodes.checkpoint: Students solve one-step and two-step linear equations by backtracking (undoing operations in reverse order).
criteria: Correctly solves a two-step linear equation using backtracking.
Identifies the inverse operations used.
Applies backtracking to multi-operation equations in the correct order.

nodes.label: Solving algebraically and verifying
nodes.checkpoint: Students solve one-variable linear equations algebraically, using the balance model, and verify the solution by substitution.
criteria: Solves a one-variable linear equation algebraically with correct steps shown.
Verifies the solution by substituting back into the original equation.
Does not skip verification.

descriptors.title: Graphs of functions
descriptors.description: describe relationships between variables represented in graphs of functions from authentic data

nodes.label: Reading and interpreting graphs of real data
nodes.checkpoint: Students read values from graphs of authentic data and describe what the graph shows in context.
criteria: Reads specific values from a graph accurately.
Describes trends (increasing, decreasing, constant, periodic) in contextual terms.
Does not interpret a graph in isolation from its axes labels and units.

nodes.label: Identifying and describing the relationship between variables
nodes.checkpoint: Students identify and describe the relationship between the two variables in a graph, including direction, rate of change, and any notable features.
criteria: Describes the relationship between variables including direction and approximate rate of change.
Identifies and interprets at least one notable feature (e.g. peak, plateau, sudden change) in context.
Uses the variable names from the axes in their description.

descriptors.title: Tables and graphs from patterns
descriptors.description: generate tables of values from visually growing patterns or the rule of a function; describe and plot these relationships on the Cartesian plane

nodes.label: Generating tables of values from patterns
nodes.checkpoint: Students identify the rule in a visually growing pattern and use it to generate a table of values.
criteria: Correctly generates a table of values from a growing pattern.
Identifies the rule that generates the values.
Can find the value for a term not shown in the original pattern.

nodes.label: Generating tables from function rules
nodes.checkpoint: Students generate a table of ordered pairs from a given function rule and identify the relationship between input and output values.
criteria: Correctly generates a table of ordered pairs from a given function rule.
Labels the table with input (x) and output (y) columns.
Does not substitute the same value for both x and y.

nodes.label: Plotting and describing relationships on the Cartesian plane
nodes.checkpoint: Students plot ordered pairs from a table of values on the Cartesian plane and describe the resulting relationship.
criteria: Correctly plots ordered pairs from a table on the Cartesian plane.
Draws a line through plotted points for a linear relationship.
Describes the relationship shown in the graph using appropriate language.

descriptors.title: Manipulate formulas
descriptors.description: manipulate formulas involving several variables using digital tools, and describe the effect of systematic variation in the values of the variables

nodes.label: Systematic variation of one variable
nodes.checkpoint: Students vary one variable in a formula while holding others constant, and describe the effect on the output.
criteria: Correctly varies one variable while holding others constant.
Describes the effect of the variation on the output in words.
Uses a table or digital tool to organise the systematic variation.

nodes.label: Describing effects of variation across multiple variables
nodes.checkpoint: Students describe how changing each variable in a multi-variable formula affects the output, and identify which variables have the greatest effect.
criteria: Correctly describes the effect of changing each variable on the output.
Identifies which variable produces the largest change in output for an equal proportional variation.
Uses digital tool output systematically rather than performing isolated calculations.

descriptors.title: Area of triangles and parallelograms
descriptors.description: solve problems involving the area of triangles and parallelograms using established formulas and appropriate units

nodes.label: Deriving the triangle area formula
nodes.checkpoint: Students understand why the area of a triangle is half the area of a related rectangle or parallelogram, and can state the formula A = ½bh.
criteria: States the area formula for a triangle and explains its derivation.
Correctly identifies the base and corresponding perpendicular height.
Does not confuse the slant side with the perpendicular height.

nodes.label: Applying area formulas to triangles and parallelograms
nodes.checkpoint: Students calculate the area of triangles and parallelograms using established formulas, selecting appropriate units.
criteria: Correctly calculates the area of a triangle using A = ½bh.
Correctly calculates the area of a parallelogram.
Uses appropriate units and converts if necessary.

descriptors.title: Volume of right prisms
descriptors.description: solve problems involving the volume of right prisms including rectangular and triangular prisms, using established formulas and appropriate units

nodes.label: Volume as cross-section area times height
nodes.checkpoint: Students understand that the volume of any right prism equals the area of its cross-section multiplied by its height.
criteria: States that V = Ah for right prisms and explains what A and h represent.
Correctly identifies the cross-section and its area for a given prism.
Does not confuse the total surface area with the cross-sectional area.

nodes.label: Calculating volume of rectangular and triangular prisms
nodes.checkpoint: Students calculate the volume of rectangular and triangular right prisms using V = Ah with appropriate units.
criteria: Correctly calculates volume for both rectangular and triangular prisms.
Uses appropriate cubic units.
Converts between units where required (e.g. cm³ to litres).

descriptors.title: Pi and circle features
descriptors.description: describe the relationship between π and the features of circles including the circumference, radius and diameter

nodes.label: Features of circles and their relationships
nodes.checkpoint: Students can identify and name the features of a circle (radius, diameter, circumference, chord) and state that diameter = 2 × radius.
criteria: Correctly identifies and labels all key features of a circle.
States that diameter = 2 × radius and applies it correctly.
Does not confuse radius with diameter.

nodes.label: Discovering π as a constant ratio
nodes.checkpoint: Students investigate the ratio C/d for multiple circles and recognise that it is always approximately 3.14 — this constant is π.
criteria: Measures and calculates C/d for at least two circles and observes the result is approximately 3.14.
States that π ≈ 3.14 and explains what it represents.
Does not treat π as just a button on a calculator without understanding its meaning.

nodes.label: Using π to calculate circumference and diameter
nodes.checkpoint: Students use C = πd (or C = 2πr) to calculate the circumference given the diameter or radius, and rearrange to find diameter given circumference.
criteria: Correctly calculates circumference given diameter or radius.
Correctly finds diameter given circumference.
Uses an appropriate approximation for π and specifies it.

descriptors.title: Angles with parallel lines
descriptors.description: identify corresponding, alternate and co-interior relationships between angles formed when parallel lines are crossed by a transversal; use them to solve problems and explain reasons

nodes.label: Parallel lines and transversals
nodes.checkpoint: Students identify parallel lines and transversals in diagrams and name the eight angles formed.
criteria: Correctly identifies and labels the eight angles formed.
Correctly identifies at least one example of each: corresponding, alternate, co-interior pair.
Does not confuse vertically opposite angles with the parallel line angle relationships.

nodes.label: Properties of corresponding, alternate and co-interior angles
nodes.checkpoint: Students state and apply the angle properties: corresponding angles are equal, alternate angles are equal, co-interior angles are supplementary.
criteria: States each angle property correctly.
Calculates missing angles using the correct property.
Does not apply the equal-angle property to co-interior pairs.

nodes.label: Using angle reasoning to solve problems
nodes.checkpoint: Students solve multi-step angle problems involving parallel lines, giving geometric reasons for each step.
criteria: Solves a multi-step angle problem correctly.
States a geometric reason for each step.
Does not assume angle values without justification.

descriptors.title: Angle sum of triangles
descriptors.description: demonstrate that the interior angle sum of a triangle in the plane is 180° and apply this to determine the interior angle sum of other shapes and the size of unknown angles

nodes.label: Demonstrating the triangle angle sum
nodes.checkpoint: Students demonstrate, using concrete or dynamic methods, that the interior angles of any triangle sum to 180°.
criteria: Demonstrates the angle sum of a triangle is 180° using at least one method.
States the property applies to all triangles.
Measures angles in a triangle and verifies the sum is approximately 180°.

nodes.label: Interior angle sum of polygons by decomposition
nodes.checkpoint: Students use decomposition of polygons into triangles to determine the interior angle sum formula for n-sided polygons.
criteria: Correctly decomposes a polygon into triangles and calculates the interior angle sum.
States the general formula (n−2) × 180° and applies it correctly.
Can verify their result by measuring.

nodes.label: Finding unknown angles using angle sums
nodes.checkpoint: Students use triangle and polygon angle sum properties to find unknown angles, giving reasons.
criteria: Correctly finds unknown angles using angle sum properties.
States the property used as the reason for each step.
Applies the correct angle sum for the polygon type.

descriptors.title: Mathematical modelling with ratios
descriptors.description: use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving ratios; formulate problems, interpret and communicate solutions in terms of the situation, justifying choices made about the representation

nodes.label: Recognising ratio structure in measurement problems
nodes.checkpoint: Students identify when a practical measurement problem involves a ratio relationship and represent it using ratio notation.
criteria: Correctly identifies the ratio structure in a practical measurement problem.
Represents the ratio using appropriate notation.
Distinguishes part-part from part-whole ratio in context.

nodes.label: Formulating, solving and interpreting ratio models
nodes.checkpoint: Students formulate a ratio model for a practical measurement problem, solve it, and interpret and communicate the solution in terms of the original situation.
criteria: Formulates the ratio model correctly from the problem description.
Solves the problem and expresses the answer with appropriate measurement units.
Justifies the representation choice and checks the solution for reasonableness.

descriptors.title: Perfect squares and square roots
descriptors.description: describe the relationship between perfect square numbers and square roots, and use squares of numbers and square roots of perfect square numbers to solve problems

nodes.label: Squares as area models
nodes.checkpoint: Students can connect squaring a number to the area of a square with that side length, and list perfect square numbers from 1 to 144.
criteria: Lists perfect square numbers from 1² to 12² without error.
Represents a given perfect square as an area model and states its side length.
Does not confuse the square number with its root (e.g. does not say '9 squared is 3').

nodes.label: Square root as inverse operation
nodes.checkpoint: Students understand that square root is the inverse of squaring and can find the exact square root of any perfect square up to 144.
criteria: States the square root of any perfect square from 1 to 144 when prompted.
Explains in words what √25 means ('the number that when multiplied by itself gives 25').
Does not conflate squaring with multiplying by 2.

nodes.label: Locating non-perfect square roots
nodes.checkpoint: Students can identify which two consecutive integers a square root falls between for numbers that are not perfect squares.
criteria: For any given number, correctly identifies the two consecutive perfect squares it lies between.
States the corresponding square root interval (e.g. '√43 is between 6 and 7').
Explains the reasoning, not just the answer.

nodes.label: Applying square roots to problems
nodes.checkpoint: Students use the relationship between perfect square numbers and square roots to solve practical problems, including finding the side length of a square given its area.
criteria: Given the area of a square, correctly determines the side length using square root reasoning.
Solves a two-step problem involving squares and square roots in a practical context.
Checks that their answer is reasonable (e.g. side length must be positive).

descriptors.title: Prime factorisation and exponent notation
descriptors.description: represent natural numbers as products of powers of prime numbers using exponent notation

nodes.label: Exponent notation for repeated multiplication
nodes.checkpoint: Students understand exponent notation as shorthand for repeated multiplication and can convert between expanded and exponent forms.
criteria: Correctly converts between repeated multiplication and exponent notation.
States the meaning of the base and exponent in a given expression.
Does not confuse aⁿ with a×n (e.g. does not evaluate 2³ as 6).

nodes.label: Prime factorisation via factor trees
nodes.checkpoint: Students can express any natural number as a product of prime factors using a factor tree, and write the result using exponent notation.
criteria: Produces a correct factor tree and writes the result in exponent notation.
Verifies the factorisation by expanding and multiplying.
Understands that the prime factorisation of a number is unique.

nodes.label: LCM and GCD from prime factorisations
nodes.checkpoint: Students use prime factorisations to find the lowest common multiple and greatest common divisor of pairs of natural numbers.
criteria: Correctly finds LCM and GCD for a given pair using prime factorisations.
Can explain why the method works (not just apply it).
Applies LCM or GCD appropriately when presented with a contextual problem.

descriptors.title: Expanded notation and powers of 10
descriptors.description: represent natural numbers in expanded notation using place value and powers of 10

nodes.label: Powers of 10 as place value columns
nodes.checkpoint: Students connect each place value column to a power of 10 and write powers of 10 in exponent notation (10⁰=1, 10¹=10, 10²=100, etc.).
criteria: Correctly states the power of 10 corresponding to each place value column up to millions.
Writes 10⁰ = 1 and explains why.
Does not confuse the exponent with the value (e.g. does not say 10³ = 30).

nodes.label: Expanded notation using powers of 10
nodes.checkpoint: Students write any natural number in expanded notation using powers of 10 (e.g. 7000 = 7 × 10³) and convert back from expanded to standard form.
criteria: Correctly writes any given natural number in expanded notation using powers of 10.
Reconstructs a number correctly from its expanded notation.
Explains what each term in the expanded form represents.

descriptors.title: Rational numbers on a number line
descriptors.description: find equivalent representations of rational numbers and represent rational numbers on a number line

nodes.label: Equivalence and simplification of fractions
nodes.checkpoint: Students find equivalent fractions using common multiples and express fractions in simplest form using common divisors.
criteria: Generates multiple equivalent fractions for a given fraction.
Correctly simplifies a fraction to lowest terms.
Can explain why the fractions are equivalent (multiplying/dividing numerator and denominator by the same value).

nodes.label: Converting between fraction, decimal and percentage
nodes.checkpoint: Students convert fluently between fraction, decimal and percentage representations of rational numbers.
criteria: Correctly converts a given rational number between fraction, decimal and percentage forms.
Identifies when representations are equivalent without performing full conversion.
Does not confuse 0.5 with 5% (confusing decimal and percentage forms).

nodes.label: Rational numbers on the number line
nodes.checkpoint: Students place positive and negative fractions, decimals and mixed numerals accurately on a number line, including intervals other than 0–1.
criteria: Correctly places a given set of rational numbers (including negatives and mixed numerals) on a number line.
Selects and labels appropriate scale for the interval.
Correctly orders the set from least to greatest.

descriptors.title: Rounding and estimation
descriptors.description: round decimals to a given accuracy appropriate to the context and use appropriate rounding and estimation to check the reasonableness of solutions

nodes.label: Rounding decimals to specified places
nodes.checkpoint: Students round decimals to a given number of decimal places using standard rounding conventions.
criteria: Correctly rounds a decimal to a specified number of decimal places.
Applies the 'round half up' convention consistently.
Does not confuse rounding to 2 decimal places with rounding to the nearest 100.

nodes.label: Context-appropriate accuracy
nodes.checkpoint: Students choose an appropriate level of rounding for a given context and explain why that accuracy is suitable.
criteria: Selects a contextually appropriate level of decimal accuracy and justifies it.
Recognises that different contexts require different precision.
Can explain why rounding to too many places can give a false sense of precision.

nodes.label: Estimation to check reasonableness
nodes.checkpoint: Students use estimation strategies (front-end, rounding, compatible numbers) to check whether a calculated solution is reasonable.
criteria: Produces a reasonable estimate before or after computing.
Identifies whether a given answer is unreasonable based on estimation.
Explains the estimation strategy used.

descriptors.title: Four operations with rational numbers
descriptors.description: use the 4 operations with positive rational numbers including fractions, decimals and percentages to solve problems using efficient calculation strategies

nodes.label: Addition and subtraction of fractions and decimals
nodes.checkpoint: Students add and subtract fractions (including mixed numerals) and decimals fluently, using common denominators and place value alignment.
criteria: Correctly adds and subtracts fractions with unlike denominators.
Correctly adds and subtracts decimals using place value alignment.
Does not add numerators and denominators directly when adding fractions.

nodes.label: Multiplication and division of fractions and decimals
nodes.checkpoint: Students multiply and divide fractions and decimals using appropriate strategies including area models and algorithm.
criteria: Correctly multiplies two fractions and simplifies the result.
Correctly divides a fraction by a whole number or simple fraction.
Does not apply addition rules (common denominator) to multiplication.

nodes.label: Operations with percentages
nodes.checkpoint: Students calculate percentages of quantities and solve problems involving percentage increase, decrease, and finding the whole given a percentage.
criteria: Correctly finds a percentage of a quantity using an efficient method.
Solves a percentage increase or decrease problem correctly.
Selects an appropriate representation (fraction, decimal, or percentage) for efficient computation.

nodes.label: Efficient strategy selection
nodes.checkpoint: Students choose the most efficient calculation strategy for a given rational number problem, drawing on number properties and representation choices.
criteria: Selects and applies an efficient strategy (not just the standard algorithm) for a given computation.
Justifies why the chosen strategy is efficient.
Applies at least one number property (commutative, associative, distributive) explicitly.

descriptors.title: Add and subtract integers
descriptors.description: compare, order and solve problems involving addition and subtraction of integers

nodes.label: Comparing and ordering integers
nodes.checkpoint: Students compare and order integers using less-than and greater-than notation, including negative integers.
criteria: Correctly orders a set of integers including negatives.
Uses < and > notation correctly between integers.
Does not confuse the magnitude of a negative with its value (e.g. understands −10 < −1).

nodes.label: Addition and subtraction of integers
nodes.checkpoint: Students add and subtract integers using a number line and understand the effect of adding or subtracting a negative number.
criteria: Correctly adds and subtracts integers including cases with negative operands.
Interprets adding a negative number as movement in the negative direction.
Does not treat subtraction of a negative as subtraction (e.g. 5 − (−3) = 8, not 2).

descriptors.title: Ratios
descriptors.description: recognise, represent and solve problems involving ratios

nodes.label: Ratio as a relationship between quantities
nodes.checkpoint: Students recognise that a ratio expresses a multiplicative relationship between two quantities and can represent ratios using diagrams and notation.
criteria: Writes a given ratio correctly in a:b notation.
Distinguishes between part-part and part-whole interpretations of a ratio.
Represents a ratio accurately using a diagram.

nodes.label: Equivalent ratios and simplification
nodes.checkpoint: Students find equivalent ratios by scaling up and down, and express a ratio in simplest form.
criteria: Correctly simplifies a ratio to lowest terms.
Generates equivalent ratios by multiplying or dividing both parts by the same value.
Does not confuse simplifying a ratio with subtracting the same value from both parts.

nodes.label: Sharing in a given ratio
nodes.checkpoint: Students share a quantity in a given ratio and solve related problems.
criteria: Correctly shares a quantity in a two-part ratio.
Identifies the total number of parts in the ratio.
Can work backwards from a share to find the total quantity.

descriptors.title: Mathematical modelling with rational numbers
descriptors.description: use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems, involving rational numbers and percentages, including financial contexts; formulate problems, choosing representations and efficient calculation strategies, using digital tools as appropriate; interpret and communicate solutions in terms of the situation, justifying choices made about the representation

nodes.label: Formulating a model from a practical problem
nodes.checkpoint: Students identify the mathematical structure of a practical problem and choose an appropriate representation (fraction, decimal, percentage, or ratio) to model it.
criteria: Correctly identifies the operation and representation needed for a given practical problem.
States any assumptions made in setting up the model.
Does not start calculating before identifying the model structure.

nodes.label: Solving and interpreting in context
nodes.checkpoint: Students solve a mathematical model and interpret the result in terms of the original situation, checking reasonableness.
criteria: Expresses the solution in contextually appropriate terms (correct units, reasonable precision).
Checks the reasonableness of the solution using estimation.
Does not present a raw number without contextual interpretation.

nodes.label: Justifying representation choices
nodes.checkpoint: Students justify why they chose a particular representation and calculation strategy, and communicate this reasoning clearly.
criteria: Justifies representation choices with reference to the problem context and computation efficiency.
Communicates the solution process, not just the answer.
Can identify a more efficient representation when presented with an inefficient one.

descriptors.title: Sample space and probability
descriptors.description: identify the sample space for single-stage events; assign probabilities to the outcomes of these events and predict relative frequencies for related events

nodes.label: Identifying and listing sample spaces
nodes.checkpoint: Students identify the sample space for a single-stage event and list all possible outcomes systematically.
criteria: Lists a complete sample space for a given single-stage event.
Explains what sample space means.
Verifies completeness (all outcomes accounted for).

nodes.label: Assigning probabilities to outcomes
nodes.checkpoint: Students assign theoretical probabilities to outcomes of a single-stage event using P = favourable/total and express these as fractions, decimals or percentages.
criteria: Correctly assigns the probability to each outcome in a sample space.
Verifies that all probabilities sum to 1.
Expresses probability in the most appropriate form for the context.

nodes.label: Predicting relative frequencies
nodes.checkpoint: Students use theoretical probability to predict how often an outcome will occur in a given number of trials.
criteria: Correctly predicts the relative frequency for a given number of trials.
Understands that predictions are expected values, not certainties.
Can adjust predictions for non-fair devices.

descriptors.title: Repeated experiments and simulation
descriptors.description: conduct repeated chance experiments and run simulations with a large number of trials using digital tools; compare predictions about outcomes with observed results, explaining the differences

nodes.label: Running experiments and recording results
nodes.checkpoint: Students conduct repeated chance experiments and record observed frequencies systematically.
criteria: Records observed frequencies in an organised frequency table.
Calculates relative frequency from observed results.
Compares observed relative frequency to theoretical probability.

nodes.label: Law of large numbers — observed vs predicted
nodes.checkpoint: Students observe that relative frequencies become closer to theoretical probability as the number of trials increases, and explain why short-run results may differ from predictions.
criteria: States that relative frequencies approach theoretical probability as trials increase.
Explains why short-run results can differ significantly from predictions.
Does not commit the gambler's fallacy (thinking past outcomes affect future probabilities).

descriptors.title: 2D representations of 3D objects
descriptors.description: represent objects in 2 dimensions; discuss and reason about the advantages and disadvantages of different representations

nodes.label: Nets of prisms and other 3D objects
nodes.checkpoint: Students identify, draw and construct nets of prisms and other common 3D objects.
criteria: Correctly identifies valid nets for a cube and rectangular prism.
Draws a net that folds correctly to produce a given 3D object.
Does not include overlapping faces in a net.

nodes.label: Isometric and plan/elevation drawings
nodes.checkpoint: Students draw and interpret isometric drawings and plan/elevation views (front, back, side, top) of 3D objects.
criteria: Correctly draws at least two views of a 3D object.
Reconstructs a 3D object from its views.
Does not confuse view orientation (e.g. top vs front).

nodes.label: Advantages and disadvantages of different representations
nodes.checkpoint: Students reason about when each type of 2D representation is most useful and what information each preserves or loses.
criteria: States at least one advantage and one disadvantage for two different representations.
Selects an appropriate representation for a given purpose and justifies the choice.
Recognises that no single representation shows all information about a 3D object.

descriptors.title: Classifying triangles and polygons
descriptors.description: classify triangles, quadrilaterals and other polygons according to their side and angle properties; identify and reason about relationships

nodes.label: Classifying triangles by sides and angles
nodes.checkpoint: Students classify triangles as scalene, isosceles or equilateral (by sides) and as acute, right-angled or obtuse (by angles), and understand that these classifications are independent.
criteria: Correctly classifies a triangle by both side and angle properties.
Understands that the two classifications are independent.
Does not assume equilateral means right-angled.

nodes.label: Classifying quadrilaterals and their relationships
nodes.checkpoint: Students classify quadrilaterals (square, rectangle, rhombus, parallelogram, kite, trapezium) using side and angle properties, and identify hierarchical relationships.
criteria: Correctly classifies any standard quadrilateral using its properties.
States at least two hierarchical relationships between quadrilateral types.
Does not rely on orientation to classify (e.g. recognises a rotated square).

nodes.label: Classifying other polygons and reasoning about properties
nodes.checkpoint: Students classify polygons by number of sides and by regularity, and reason about properties such as line symmetry and convexity.
criteria: Correctly classifies polygons by name, regularity, and convexity.
Explains what makes a polygon regular.
Can identify whether a polygon is convex or concave and explain the difference.

descriptors.title: Transformations on the Cartesian plane
descriptors.description: describe transformations of a set of points using coordinates in the Cartesian plane, translations and reflections on an axis, and rotations about a given point

nodes.label: Translations using coordinates
nodes.checkpoint: Students translate a set of points on the Cartesian plane and describe the translation using coordinate changes.
criteria: Correctly translates a set of points and records the new coordinates.
Describes the translation in terms of horizontal and vertical movement.
Verifies that the shape is congruent to the original after translation.

nodes.label: Reflections on axes
nodes.checkpoint: Students reflect a set of points on the x-axis and y-axis and describe the transformation using coordinate rules.
criteria: Correctly reflects a set of points across the x-axis and y-axis.
States the coordinate rule for each reflection.
Does not confuse which coordinate negates for each axis.

nodes.label: Rotations about a given point
nodes.checkpoint: Students rotate a set of points about a given point (origin or other) by 90°, 180° and 270° and describe the rotation using coordinates.
criteria: Correctly rotates points by 90° and 180° about the origin.
Records the new coordinates and identifies the pattern.
Specifies direction of rotation (clockwise/counterclockwise) when describing.

descriptors.title: Algorithms for classifying shapes
descriptors.description: design and create algorithms involving a sequence of steps and decisions that will sort and classify sets of shapes according to their attributes, and describe how the algorithms work

nodes.label: Designing a classification algorithm
nodes.checkpoint: Students design a step-by-step algorithm (as a flowchart or decision tree) that classifies shapes according to their attributes.
criteria: Produces a flowchart or decision tree that correctly classifies the target shapes.
Includes decision points with clear yes/no branches.
Tests the algorithm on at least two examples and corrects any errors.

nodes.label: Describing and evaluating algorithms
nodes.checkpoint: Students describe in words how an algorithm works and evaluate its correctness by tracing through it with test cases.
criteria: Correctly traces a classification algorithm with a test input.
Identifies at least one case where a given algorithm fails (if one exists).
Explains in plain language how the algorithm works.

descriptors.title: Data acquisition and measures of centre
descriptors.description: acquire data sets for discrete and continuous numerical variables and calculate the range, median, mean and mode; make and justify decisions about which measures of central tendency provide useful insights into the nature of the distribution of data

nodes.label: Distinguishing discrete and continuous numerical variables
nodes.checkpoint: Students distinguish discrete from continuous numerical variables and understand how this affects data acquisition.
criteria: Correctly classifies given variables as discrete or continuous.
Explains the key distinction (countable vs measurable).
Identifies appropriate units and precision for a continuous variable.

nodes.label: Calculating range, median, mean and mode
nodes.checkpoint: Students calculate all four summary statistics for a given data set.
criteria: Correctly calculates range, median, mean and mode for a given data set.
Handles even-count data sets correctly for median.
Recognises and handles data sets with no mode or multiple modes.

nodes.label: Justifying which measure is most useful
nodes.checkpoint: Students reason about which measure of central tendency best describes a given distribution, considering outliers, skewness, and the purpose of the summary.
criteria: Identifies which measure best represents a given distribution and justifies the choice.
Explains the effect of outliers on mean vs median.
Selects different measures for different contexts appropriately.

descriptors.title: Data displays and distribution
descriptors.description: create different types of numerical data displays including stem-and-leaf plots using software where appropriate; describe and compare the distribution of data, commenting on the shape, centre and spread including outliers and determining the range, median, mean and mode

nodes.label: Creating stem-and-leaf plots
nodes.checkpoint: Students construct ordered stem-and-leaf plots from a data set and read values from them accurately.
criteria: Constructs an ordered stem-and-leaf plot with correct stems and leaves.
Orders the leaves within each stem.
Includes a key explaining what the stem and leaf represent.

nodes.label: Describing distribution shape, centre, spread and outliers
nodes.checkpoint: Students describe the distribution of data in terms of its shape (symmetrical, skewed), centre, spread and the presence of outliers.
criteria: Describes the shape of a distribution using appropriate vocabulary.
Identifies the appropriate measure of centre for the distribution's shape.
Identifies outliers and comments on their effect.

nodes.label: Comparing distributions
nodes.checkpoint: Students compare two distributions using displays and summary statistics, making statements about differences in shape, centre and spread.
criteria: Makes at least two comparative statements about two distributions (using statistics and display features).
States conclusions in context, not just in mathematical terms.
Does not compare individual values as if they represent the distributions.

descriptors.title: Statistical investigations
descriptors.description: plan and conduct statistical investigations involving data for discrete and continuous numerical variables; analyse and interpret distributions of data and report findings in terms of shape and summary statistics

nodes.label: Planning a statistical investigation
nodes.checkpoint: Students identify a statistical question, plan data collection (including variable type, measurement method and sample), and anticipate potential sources of bias.
criteria: Writes a clear statistical question that can be answered with data.
Identifies the variable type (discrete or continuous) and appropriate measurement method.
Identifies at least one potential source of variability in their data collection.

nodes.label: Conducting, analysing and reporting
nodes.checkpoint: Students collect data, display it appropriately, analyse the distribution using summary statistics, and report findings in terms of the statistical question.
criteria: Collects, displays and analyses data appropriate to the variable type.
Reports findings that address the original statistical question.
Uses distribution language (shape, centre, spread) in the report.

descriptors.title: Simplify linear expressions
descriptors.description: create, expand, factorise, rearrange and simplify linear expressions, applying the associative, commutative, identity, distributive and inverse properties

nodes.label: Expanding and simplifying linear expressions
nodes.checkpoint: Students expand brackets in linear expressions using the distributive property and collect like terms to simplify.
criteria: Correctly expands brackets including those with negative coefficients.
Collects like terms accurately.
Does not partially distribute (e.g. only multiply the first term).

nodes.label: Factorising linear expressions
nodes.checkpoint: Students factorise linear expressions by identifying the highest common factor and express as a product of the HCF and a bracket.
criteria: Identifies the HCF of all terms in a linear expression.
Writes the factorised form correctly.
Verifies by expanding back to the original expression.

nodes.label: Rearranging linear expressions
nodes.checkpoint: Students rearrange linear expressions and formulas using inverse operations and algebraic properties, maintaining equivalence.
criteria: Correctly rearranges a linear formula to make a specified variable the subject.
Applies inverse operations in the correct order.
Verifies the rearranged formula by substitution.

descriptors.title: Graph and solve linear equations
descriptors.description: graph linear relations on the Cartesian plane using digital tools where appropriate; solve linear equations and one-variable inequalities using graphical and algebraic techniques; verify solutions by substitution

nodes.label: Graphing linear relations including inequalities
nodes.checkpoint: Students graph linear relations of the form y = mx + b and one-variable inequalities on the Cartesian plane, identifying key features.
criteria: Correctly graphs a linear relation from a rule or table.
Identifies gradient and y-intercept from graph and equation.
Correctly represents an inequality including the boundary line convention (solid vs dashed).

nodes.label: Solving linear equations algebraically
nodes.checkpoint: Students solve linear equations of the form ax + b = cx + d algebraically, including equations requiring expansion, and verify by substitution.
criteria: Solves a linear equation with unknowns on both sides correctly.
Verifies the solution by substitution.
Does not leave the unknown on both sides after the first step.

nodes.label: Solving inequalities and using graphical methods
nodes.checkpoint: Students solve one-variable inequalities algebraically and verify using graphical methods; represent solutions on a number line.
criteria: Solves a one-variable inequality correctly including sign reversal where needed.
Represents the solution on a number line with correct open/closed endpoint.
Verifies the solution graphically or by substitution.

descriptors.title: Model with linear functions
descriptors.description: use mathematical modelling to solve applied problems involving linear relations, including financial contexts; formulate problems with linear functions, choosing a representation; interpret and communicate solutions in terms of the situation, reviewing the appropriateness of the model

nodes.label: Formulating linear models
nodes.checkpoint: Students identify a linear relationship in a practical context, formulate it as a function y = mx + b, and identify the meaning of gradient and intercept in context.
criteria: Correctly identifies gradient and intercept from a practical context.
Formulates the linear function in equation form.
Interprets m and b in terms of the problem context.

nodes.label: Solving, interpreting and reviewing the model
nodes.checkpoint: Students solve a linear model for a given value, interpret the solution in context, and evaluate whether the model is appropriate for the situation.
criteria: Uses the linear model correctly to answer a specific question.
States the solution in contextually appropriate terms.
Identifies at least one limitation or domain restriction of the model.

descriptors.title: Experiment with linear functions
descriptors.description: experiment with linear functions and relations using digital tools, making and testing conjectures and generalising emerging patterns

nodes.label: Effect of gradient parameter on linear graphs
nodes.checkpoint: Students investigate the effect of varying the gradient m in y = mx + b on the graph and generalise the relationship between m and steepness/direction.
criteria: Correctly describes the effect of varying m on the graph.
States a general rule for positive, negative and zero gradient.
Tests the conjecture with at least one new value.

nodes.label: Effect of intercept and generalising patterns
nodes.checkpoint: Students investigate the effect of varying the y-intercept b, and generalise patterns including the behaviour of parallel lines.
criteria: Correctly states the effect of varying b on the graph.
Identifies that lines with equal gradient are parallel.
States a generalisation supported by evidence from their investigation.

descriptors.title: Area and perimeter of composite shapes
descriptors.description: solve problems involving the area and perimeter of irregular and composite shapes using appropriate units

nodes.label: Decomposing composite shapes for area
nodes.checkpoint: Students decompose a composite shape into known shapes and calculate the total area by summing component areas.
criteria: Correctly identifies a valid decomposition of the composite shape.
Calculates each component area accurately.
Combines areas correctly (adding or subtracting as required).

nodes.label: Perimeter and area of irregular shapes
nodes.checkpoint: Students estimate and calculate the perimeter and area of irregular shapes using measurement approximation strategies.
